name: EliasDB
tagline: Lightweight Go graph database with GraphQL, an SQL-like query language, full-text search and scripting.
description: EliasDB is a self-contained graph database written from scratch in Go by Matthias Ladkau, with gorilla/websocket as its only dependency. It stores key-value nodes connected by typed edges, separated into partitions, on top of its own transactional key-value store, and every stored value is indexed for full-text phrase search. You query it with EQL, an SQL-like traversal language, or through a GraphQL API that also supports subscriptions; the standalone server adds HTTPS, user management, a REST API with Swagger docs and a web terminal, and it can also be embedded as a Go library. The ECAL scripting language hooks database events to write backend logic. Feature work stopped at 1.4.0 (August 2022); since then only dependency updates have landed.
statusNote: Last feature release 1.4.0 (August 2022); only dependency bumps since. Clustering is documented as experimental.

scale.notes: Single node in practice; an experimental peer-to-peer cluster mode replicates data with eventual, last-writer-wins consistency.

strengths: Single static Go binary or embeddable library with almost no third-party dependencies
Full-text phrase search over every stored value with no extra setup
GraphQL queries, mutations and subscriptions out of the box
ECAL event scripting lets you write backend logic inside the database
Cascading deletes and partitions keep graph hygiene simple
weaknesses: Single maintainer and no feature releases since 2022
Clustering is experimental and only eventually consistent
EQL is proprietary; no Cypher, Gremlin or SPARQL support
Small community and few production references
useCases: Embedded graph storage inside Go applications
Prototyping GraphQL backends over a graph model
Small knowledge graphs or personal data hubs with search
notIdealFor: Large-scale or highly available graph workloads
Teams that need Cypher or Gremlin compatibility
